items.title: arm: applied regression helpers
items.evidence: Partial (2026-11-21, merged 9e1b3e122; Windows fixtures pass, score from agent reports not re-audited): Merged worktree-wf_3d9b6b36-bf7-18 (clean, no conflicts). Fixed the bayesglm inverse.gaussian seed 21804 gap: the 3-ulp IRLS drift started at iteration 9 because pow15 (eta^1.5, 1/mu^2 link) was correctly rounded while R on Windows rounds the x87 extended result a second time. pow15 now uses armx87.r64 (same model as exp_r/log_r). Seed 21804 now matches R to the last bit (coef, dispersion, draws), and its draws are in the oracle at rel 1e-9 / abs 1e-11 (exclusion removed in armglm.R, armglmsim.json regenerated). Also found that glm/bayesglm sim draws are already checked coefficient by coeffici Remaining: (1) sim() for merMod from Neper's own lmer fit (simmer, 99 cases) and se.fixef/se.ranef (semer, 34 cases) are only checked at rel 2e-3 with abs 1e-4 to 1e-6 in tests/oracle/armmer.json; only the R-theta v | (2) sim for glmer (80 simglmer cases) is fed R's theta, beta, u and working weights because Neper has no glmer fit, so only the draw path is verified; either add a glmer fit or state in the Acceptance tha | (3) armglmsim covers glm/bayesglm sim coefficient by coefficient only on fits where V.beta matches R's bit for bit (scripts/r_oracle/groups/armglm.R line 62 filters out the roughly one third where LAPACK  | (4) dicmer is checked at rel/abs 1e-5 (17 cases) with no R-side reason recorded; tighten to 1e-8 or document why in scripts/r_oracle/groups/armmer.R. | (5) Linux has not been run and the notes say oracle_armpolr fails against the Windows-generated oracle; run all eight fixtures on Linux and make oracle_armpolr pass or regenerate it platform-independently | (6) sim for merMod: simmer/semer (sim, se.fixef, se.ranef from Neper's own lmer fit) still at rel 2e-3 / abs 1e-4 to 1e-6 because lmer's bobyqa stops about 1e-4 from the optimum; needs a port of NLopt BOB | (7) sim for glmer (simglmer) is driven by R's theta, beta, u and working weights; Neper has no glmer fit (PIRLS plus optimiser), so only the draw path is checked (1e-9), not a Neper-made fit. Not started. | (8) Linux batch 2026-11-22 (WSL Ubuntu-24.04, a Linux stage-1 built by the C bootstrap, and re-run with a Linux release stage-2): six of the eight fixtures pass - oracle_arm, oracle_armextra, oracle_armglm, oracle_armglmsim, oracle_armmer and oracle_armsim all exit 0 - and all eight pass on x64-windows with a release stage-2. Two fail on Linux only. oracle_armnum fails its 323 exact qcauchy_r cases (rel 0, abs 0) by one ulp, for example libm(9, 0.31300409603863955) answers -0.6658903459214698 against R's -0.6658903459214697, so qcauchy_r (through armtan.cr_tan_pos) is not bit-identical across hosts even though it is pure double-double arithmetic. oracle_armpolr fails several simpolr cases by a wide margin (seed 91662, p=0.20757602830417454 answers -15.765400253161364 against R's -5.427186422321726), so the simulated-draw path diverges on glibc as well. Both failures reproduce with the Linux release stage-2, so they are not a debug/release difference, and they are the remaining Linux gap. Narrowing later the same day (D7743): the same release compiler cross-emitting x64-linux (`neper-rel.exe emit-executable ... x64 linux`) reproduces both failures byte for byte, so they are decided by the target, not by the compiler that built the fixture. For oracle_armnum the cause is by design: `lib/e/algo/stat/armtan.linux.e` calls libm's own tan and atan (and the Windows variant calls ucrtbase's), so qcauchy_r, atan_c and pcauchy_c track each host's R, while tests/oracle/armnum.json records Windows R's doubles at rel 0 and abs 0. For oracle_armpolr the bpolr fit cases pass on Linux and only simpolr fails, so the fit path is portable and the draw path (`ag.sim_draws` through polr_vcov's SVD) is what still diverges.

items.title: VIM: missing-value imputation
items.evidence: Partial. e.algo.stat.vimpkg.knn_impute (one numeric variable, complete distance columns, Gower range-scaled distance, median or mean of k donors, ties by row order) equals VIM 7.3.1 kNN on Windows (oracle_vim, 40 values; it also passes on x64-linux under WSL in 1 s, 2026-11-22). vimpkg.knn_impute_mixed (2026-11-22) equals VIM::kNN over mixed numeric and categorical distance columns in 30 exact oracle cases: a categorical distance column answers 0 or 1, a categorical target takes maxCat's most frequent donor code, the numeric columns keep the range scaling over the whole table (gowerD pools the donors and the rows to impute, which is every row), and the distance is the mean over the p - 1 distance columns (VIM's default weights are all one). oracle_vim_knn_mixed passes on x64-windows and x64-linux (generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_knn_mixed.R, about 1 s), and ignoring the categorical distance fails 12 of the 30 cases. Missing values in the distance columns are covered too (2026-11-22, D7747): gowerD replaces each one with its column's largest prepared value plus one, computed after the range scaling over the pooled donors and impute rows, and an all-missing column answers 1; 30 further exact cases (oracle_vim_knn_missing, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_knn_missing.R, mixed columns, one to four missing values in a distance column and sometimes a whole column missing, a numeric or categorical target) pass on x64-windows and x64-linux, and replacing that fill with the column maximum fails 12 of them. Several targets in one call are covered as well (2026-11-22, D7748): vimpkg.knn_impute_multi fills the columns in `variable` order and a later target's distances use the earlier ones' imputed values (VIM's useImputedDist = TRUE), with 30 exact cases whose first target is missing in 20-40% of the rows and correlated with the second (oracle_vim_knn_multi, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_knn_multi.R) passing on x64-windows and x64-linux; reversing the imputation order fails 12 of them. vimpkg.aggr_counts (2026-11-22, D7749) covers VIM::aggr's counts part (plot = FALSE): the missing values per column, the missingness patterns of the rows in table() order, their counts and their percentages, where a pattern is a bitmask with the first column most significant so ascending masks are VIM's lexicographic a:b:c order; 30 exact cases (oracle_vim_aggr, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_aggr.R) pass on x64-windows and x64-linux, and flipping the bit order fails 12 of them. vimpkg.hotdeck (2026-11-22) equals VIM::hotdeck over every numeric column with variable = NULL, ord_var = NULL (the runif(n) random row order from the seed), domain_var = NULL and imp_var = FALSE: 30 oracle cases (12-45 rows, 2-5 columns, up to five missing in one column) match exactly (rel 0, abs 0) on x64-windows and on x64-linux under WSL (oracle_vim_hotdeck, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_hotdeck.R, about 1 s each). The port follows imputeHD's own rules (D7745): applicability is a snapshot of the original matrix, so a value imputed earlier in the same pass is never a donor; the donor is position - add in 1-based positions, plus n when that falls below 1, and a donor outside 1..n simply does not match rather than wrapping again; the first donor is the previous position, or the second position for the first row; and the fixture accumulates its weighted sum in the same order as R's loop, because R's sum() uses a long double accumulator and would differ in the last bits. Mutating the initial donor rule to position - 2 fails 12 cases. Remaining: ordered and semi-continuous variables, weights, donor conditions, the weightDist and addRandom options, and maxCat's random tie-break (this port takes the lowest code on a tie and the generator keeps only draws whose answer is stable over two seeds); hotdeck's domain_var, donorcond, ord_var, impNA = FALSE and the give-up-after-min(50, n) random donor, and the per-variable tables and plot data of aggr; matrixplot data, irmi and regressionImp are not started. Acceptance, equal to VIM under set.seed: kNN with Gower distance and aggregation choices, hotdeck, irmi, regressionImp, aggr summaries, matrixplot data.

items.title: e.gfx.cssvalue has no viewport-dynamic length unit, so min() over dvh does not resolve
items.evidence: Open. With C286 landed gfx_cssvalue emits and runs, and stops on `min(abs(360in), min(16pt, 100dvh))`. Its reference answer is {v:0, u:"px", o:0, p:null} -- a plain zero length whose to_px resolution is null -- while the fixture's check fails, and the likeliest reason is that css.parse_length answers not-good because LengthUnit is {Px, Pt, Em, Rem, Ex, Percent, Vw, Vh, Vmin, Vmax, Ch, Lh} with no viewport-dynamic unit, so `100dvh` is not a length at all. Whether the reference reaches 0 by treating an unknown basis as zero (so min(16pt, 0) is 0 and min(abs(360in), 0) is 0) or by clamping is the thing to establish from Vaper's Dart parser before choosing between adding the dvh family to the enum and matching the zero-basis reading. Everything after this case is unmeasured, since the fixture stops at the first mismatch. Acceptance: gfx_cssvalue runs to completion, and the fixture's remaining cases agree with the reference.

items.title: NeperOS stage 2: the kernel as an AVF guest on a Pixel (crosvm bring-up)
items.evidence: Opened by D2143 when C103 closed D2119 stage 1. Acceptance (D2119 stage 2): the same microkernel boots as an Android Virtualization Framework guest that crosvm starts with the Linux arm64 boot protocol -- device tree in x0, GICv3, PSCI 1.0, an ns16550 serial console, and virtio console, block and vsock over PCI -- first under crosvm, then on a retail Pixel via `adb shell vm run` as a non-protected VM. Device addresses are read from the device tree, never hard-coded; the virtio-pci transport already serves both. Done (D2144): the ns16550/8250 console -- neperos/src/ns16550.e drives the 8250 (THR at 0, LSR at 5 bit 5), the kernel picks it vs PL011 from the stdout uart node's `compatible` (ns16550a for crosvm, arm,pl011 for virt), base and reg-shift from the device tree; console_write and the console server's device_write dispatch by a boot-set flag. Written to crosvm's actual source (aarch64/src/fdt.rs: compatible ns16550a, reg=<addr size>, no reg-shift => shift 0) and regression-verified under QEMU virt (the tree selects PL011, all stage-1 marks pass, ns16550 path inert). Also extracted crosvm's aarch64 memory map from source (RAM 0x80000000, GIC/PCI bases). BLOCKER confirmed (D2144): crosvm is built and runs in this WSL but is KVM-only with no CPU emulation, and the host is x86-64, so it cannot run the aarch64 kernel (rejected as a bad bzImage). Verifying the crosvm/AVF boot -- and the remaining pieces, a virtio-vsock driver and the crosvm memory-map boot -- needs an aarch64 host (a Pixel via adb, or an aarch64 Linux box with KVM); surfaced to the user as a resource decision. Advanced (D2145): the EL0 user window moved to the top of the 39-bit space (index 511, VA 0x7FC0000000) so it no longer collides with crosvm's RAM at 0x80000000, which would otherwise have unmapped the kernel from every user space on the first trap; QEMU-verified -- kernel boots, every EL0 server runs, isolation holds (thread W faults at 0x7FC0040000, X at kernel RAM 0x40000000, Q at ECAM 0x4010000000). The chosen aarch64 host is an AWS Graviton bare-metal instance (only *.metal exposes /dev/kvm for crosvm's KVM backend); the account's configured AWS credentials are invalid and await refresh. The kernel image already carries a valid arm64 Image header. VERIFIED ON REAL HARDWARE (D2146, AWS a1.metal Graviton bare-metal with /dev/kvm): the kernel boots under crosvm/KVM, reads crosvm's DTB (RAM 0x80000000, GICv3, ns16550 at 0x3f8), turns the MMU on and runs the whole EL0/capability suite -- D2145 confirmed, thread W faults at the relocated window 0x7FC0040000. Two crosvm-vs-QEMU gaps found and fixed: crosvm's PCI host is CAM (pci-host-cam-generic, shifts bus<<16/slot<<11/fn<<8) not ECAM, now detected by compatible with a cam flag in pci.Host; and a virtio device's BAR is the one its capabilities name (BAR0 on crosvm, pre-assigned; BAR4 on QEMU, guest-assigned), now discovered and mapped at its real size instead of a hard-coded BAR4/64KB. All three drivers then run under crosvm: entropy returns 8 bytes, block reads/writes sector 0, console writes a virtio-console port; QEMU's ECAM path unchanged (stage-1 boot still green). D2147 then closed the last crosvm functional gap: the EL0 page mappings were global (missing the nG bit), so on a real Cortex-A72 (not QEMU's interpreter) a thread's USER_BASE TLB entry served another thread after the ASID-only context switch, making the console-server client read a neighbour's 0xCD poison and a round-printer re-run. Marking the EL0 leaf descriptors non-global fixed it; the WHOLE stage-2 demo now runs clean under crosvm/KVM on AWS a1.metal -- all three virtio drivers, the capability/isolation threads, `console server up` over the P->K server, `all threads done` and a PSCI power-off with exit 0 -- and QEMU's stage-1 boot is byte-unchanged. D2149 added the virtio-vsock driver (EL0 server T): vsock_connect sets up the three queues (rx/tx/event), reads the guest CID from device config (passed via a new aux slot 5), transmits a STREAM REQUEST to host CID 2, and reads the reply. Verified on AWS a1.metal under crosvm `--vsock cid=3` over /dev/vhost-vsock -- no listener gave op 3 (RST), a Python AF_VSOCK listener on port 1234 gave op 2 (RESPONSE) with the host logging the accept from (3, 1024), a full round trip. QEMU has no vsock device so T is skipped and stage 1 is unchanged. The whole crosvm device list (console, block, vsock over PCI) is now done. Remaining before score 1: the same kernel on a retail Pixel via `adb shell vm run`. NeperOS stages 3 (bare-metal Pixel 6) and 4 follow (D2119).

items.title: macOS notices through UNUserNotificationCenter: removal, replacement and actions

items.title: macOS window system: accessibility, input methods, close veto, live resize, Retina
items.evidence: Done 2026-10-25 and 2026-10-26 (live resize, D5856: os.window_on_resize registers a handler the window delegate's windowDidResize: calls from AppKit's tracking loop with the new pixel size; macos_window_resize on aarch64 and x64 resizes a window from code, which takes the same path; Unsupported on the other hosts): the close button is a request answered through a window delegate (D5222, macos_window_close); the published accessibility tree is NSAccessibilityElements under the content view (D5223, macos_accessibility); input methods commit text (D5229, macos_text_input). The content view's class (NeperTextView, made at run time over the view's own class) answers the text input protocol: insertText:replacementRange: turns committed text, from an NSString or an NSAttributedString, into Text events; setMarkedText, unmarkText, hasMarkedText, markedRange and selectedRange hold a composition's state (marked text is not shown, since a window event has no preedit kind: that is an API change for every host); firstRectForCharacterRange answers a point in the window's top left for the candidate window; doCommandBySelector: is ignored; the view accepts first responder, so the window has an input context. A key with an input method selected (its source id has "inputmethod" in it) goes through interpretKeyEvents:, a plain layout's key keeps its own characters as before (a synthetic key event does not come back from the input context synchronously, so the layout path stays direct). macos_text_input calls the input method's methods by hand: an accented letter and a kana become Text events, marked text produces none, committing clears the mark; aarch64 and x64, corpus 1109. Not done: a real input method composing Japanese, Chinese or Korean and its candidate window's place (C192); preedit display; focus, set-value and selection requests, tables, relations and live regions in the accessibility elements, and a real VoiceOver reading the tree (C192); native-resolution checks on a real Retina display (C192). A Retina scale change between displays needs no delegate method: every poll re-reads backingScaleFactor and the content size in pixels, so moving a window to a display of another scale shows up as a Resize with the new pixel size, and window_metrics reports the new scale_percent. Still to see on a real Mac: a drag of an edge by a person repainting smoothly through the handler.

items.title: macOS verification on real hardware: what the CI runners cannot do
items.evidence: The checklist is a program, written 2026-10-25 (D5228) and compiled for both architectures but never run: tests/macos/manual/main.e. Build it on the Mac (neper-self emit-executable tests/macos/manual/main.e . aarch64 macos manual; x64 on an Intel Mac) and run ./manual from a Terminal: it goes through one check at a time, says what to do, waits where a person is needed, and writes PASS, FAIL or skipped lines to ~/neper-manual-results.txt. It covers: the window's Retina scale, a menu-bar icon's left and right click, a pop-up menu choice, a global shortcut press (Control-Option-Shift-F12), the Open panel with two files and the Save panel's name and .txt, a drop from Finder, the clipboard in TextEdit, a notice banner, a Dock menu task and the 50% badge, Finder starting a program for an associated file, the print panel's range and copies, the camera permission, Touch ID where enrolled, the screen capture size, and VoiceOver reading a published tree and pressing its button. Not covered by it (a program cannot drive them): a real pointer drag out of a window into Finder, a notarized bundle opened on a clean Mac (C191), live resize while dragging an edge and IME composition (C190), a Metal or MoltenVK device run (C193). Done when it has been run on an Apple-silicon Mac and an Intel Mac and its results are recorded here. Handover fold 2026-11-19: also record the real-GPU Metal answers: subnormals preserved, a single 1 GiB buffer reads back, seq_cst and atomic_thread_fence compile; update C193. Consequence still open: the three real-GPU answers decide whether the limits (no DenormPreserve, 256 MiB heaps, relaxed-only atomics) belong to the runners or to Metal itself, so tag each limit in C193 as runner or Metal after the run.

items.title: macOS GPU: a Metal backend for e.gpu (the Vulkan fixtures cannot run on a Mac)
items.evidence: Phase 1 done 2026-10-25 (D5231): e.gpu.metal, the runtime alone. Phase 2 2026-10-26: src/msl.e, the MSL emitter (D5838; kernel as a switch state machine over heap offsets that reconverges by lowest block, precise::divide/sqrt, fast math off, D5840 32-bit relaxed atomics, D5852 subgroups) and e.gpu's Metal backend (D5839): on a macOS target a kernel's K$spirv carries MSL, Backend.Metal opens a device with a 256 MiB shared heap, buffers are heap ranges, launch_metal runs the SPIR-V launch ABI over it, faults come back through the fault block. Verified on Metal on aarch64 and x64: macos_metal_emitted, macos_metal_exact, macos_gpu_metal, macos_metal_atomics, macos_metal_subgroup (every word equal to the CPU backend's); the emitter's saxpy, loops and exact float are pinned in tests/conformance/msl; the full macOS corpus passes (1130/1130 on both). D5853: a heap larger than 256 MiB read back wrong on the runners. D5892: up to four launches in flight with their own fault blocks (the CPU queues ahead of the GPU; the GPU still runs them in order). D5878: up to four 256 MiB heaps, about 1 GiB of buffers (a single buffer still under 256 MiB). D5875: gpu.launch on Metal commits without waiting (the next call into the device finishes it and reports the fault), so the CPU can work while the GPU runs. Remaining: stronger atomic orders (Metal 3.1 has no fence), 64-bit atomics and subgroup operations on 64-bit values, switch and helper calls (SPIR-V has neither), the Windows and Linux suites for the shared compiler change. Gap list (handover fold 2026-11-19): 64-bit subgroup operations; switch and non-inlined helper calls in kernels; the Lost path is read, not run; launches are still serialized on the GPU; Metal has no f64, so SPIR-V f64 divide/sqrt (C095) cannot be checked on a Mac.

items.title: NeperOS shell 3: the e.os surface on NeperOS (os.neperos.e)
items.evidence: Queued by D2148. Acceptance: an `os` variant for target `aarch64 neperos` over NeperOS system calls -- memory from untyped/frame capabilities, threads, monotonic time from the counter and wall time from the RTC the device tree names (PL031 on virt), file I/O through the C106 server, stdout and stderr through the console server; e.io, e.fs, e.time, e.thread and e.fmt compile unchanged for NeperOS, and their existing fixtures that need no network pass under QEMU. BEGUN D2154 (lib/e/os.neperos.e): the e.os surface is intrinsic-based (compiler seeds open/read/write/close/seek/stdout/stderr/exit/threads/clock into e.os; the per-target variant file adds helpers), and NeperOS had no variant -- it fell back to the types-only os.e. New os.neperos.e is the variant project.select_source picks for a neperos os (a variant is the whole module: full type block + ErrorKind/ErrorDetail + NATIVE_SEPARATOR + read_detail/write_detail over the seeded read/write). e.io now compiles and RUNS unchanged on NeperOS, verified on QEMU both hosts: io_test.e reaches os.stdout() + a Writer via io.print (not the console primitive), prints two lines, exit 0; fixtures in run.ps1/run.sh. Existing neperos programs (init, shell/fs servers) unaffected (seeded intrinsics + base types only). e.time DONE (D2155): os.clock lowered to kernel syscall 13 -- monotonic from the virtual counter converted to ns, wall from the PL031 RTC the device tree names, verified on QEMU both hosts (time_test.e: elapsed ns across a spin + a 2026 wall timestamp). e.fmt DONE (D2156): the 45 fmt codecs are pure (no os primitive), so the variant + e.io carry them -- fmt_test.e encodes a struct with json.encode[T] to an e.io Writer, verified both hosts. e.thread DONE (D2157): os.thread_create spawns a thread in the same address space on a kernel-mapped stack (vm.map_stack in the spare L3 entries above the program window), join reuses the reap syscall, detach is syscall 15; a by-pointer Thread arg caused a non-blocking-join race (99 on Windows QEMU, 0 on Linux) until the wrapper dereferenced it, now 5/5 on each host. e.fs DONE (D2158): file I/O through the C106 server -- un-seed open/read/write/close/seek/readdir for neperos, add a console_write intrinsic for stdout, and write the file surface in os.neperos.e as a client-side handle model over fsproto IPC (open/read/write/close/stat/mkdir/remove real, symlink/rename/dirs/env Unsupported); fs_efs.e writes+reads /hello through the server, both hosts. ALL FIVE MODULES (e.io/e.time/e.fmt/e.thread/e.fs) now compile+run on NeperOS. Last 0.1 (thread_create/join/detach), e.fs (the ~40 path/dir/stat functions over the C106 server), e.fmt breadth, and porting the existing lib fixtures to run under QEMU. Last 0.1: stdout through the EL0 console server (now the kernel console write); the Unsupported fs ops the flat C106 server cannot serve; and porting the lib modules' own existing fixtures to NeperOS beyond the one-per-module here. D2183: e.fmt BREADTH -- fmt_test.e now also writes two rows through e.fmt.csv (a header and a data row, the default comma/LF dialect) after the json encode, so the serial reads `fmt csv: x,y,label` then `3,7,neperos`; a second pure e.fmt codec runs unchanged on NeperOS, identical on both QEMU hosts (8.2 WSL, 11.1 Windows). Built and verified with a worktree-local neper-self (~17s via the Windows bootstrap) because the shared one had been swapped by a concurrent session to a divergent line lacking this worktree's D2158 write-seed guard (resolve.e:436 keeps open/read/write/close/seek out of the seeded intrinsics for neperos so the variant defines them). D2184: a THIRD codec -- fmt_test.e also encodes the struct through e.fmt.ini (flat key=value: `x=3`/`y=7`/`label=neperos`), so three pure e.fmt codecs (json/csv/ini) run unchanged on NeperOS, identical on both QEMU hosts. Boundary found: only the SHELL boot is verifiable here; the gpu/DRIVER boot faults at the program's first instruction (unexpected exception 0x08, far 0x10000000000, exit 0x87) for every driver program incl. the unmodified, previously-green gpu_test/calc_app/clock_app -- the same binaries run under the shell boot. Two independent compilers (c103b self-host rebuilt today + build/windows/neper.exe), both from the divergent C103/master line that overwrote the shared build/, produce the IDENTICAL fault; no fa07c7d0-line compiler is available and one cannot be built here (frozen bootstrap lacks capacity, WSL crashes on the self-host build, Windows bootstrap needs absent MSVC). So the gpu-boot C107 fixtures and the C112-C114 app-face rendering are unverifiable until the branch lands on master / a matching toolchain is restored -- a coordination state, not a code defect. D2185: e.thread GROUP -- thread_test.e now also runs thread.spawn_all/join_all (three workers over three contexts, one barrier; each write checked after join_all), serial `thread group of 3 joined`, both QEMU hosts. This also sharpens the boundary: the toolchain miscompile is NARROW -- thread_test drives os.thread_create + vm.map_stack (page-table code of the same family as the faulting map_range_el0) and runs correctly on the shell boot with the same neper-self that faults the driver boot, so only the device-MMIO driver-boot path is affected; the rest of the e.os surface (e.io/e.time/e.fmt/e.thread spawn+join+group) stays verifiable. D2186: e.time CALENDAR breadth -- time_test.e now converts the wall timestamp to a civil date via time.to_date (days_from_civil/civil_from_days floor-division math) and prints `time date 2026-10-7`, proving the calendar path runs on NeperOS beyond the raw clock read; fixtures assert a `time date 20xx-` pattern, both QEMU hosts. Confirmed the C113/C114 faces render via e.gpu's CPU backend (no real GPU) but need the 16MB out-of-window arena, which both the driver boot and start_process's bigarena path get through the one miscompiled map_range_el0 (main.e:85), and the 2MB in-window cap is far too small -- so the faces are sound but verifiable only with a matching toolchain. D2187: e.io BUFFER round-trip -- io_test.e now, after the two stdout prints, writes seven bytes through an io.SliceWriter and reads them back through an io.SliceReader over the written portion (bytes and both counts checked), serial `io roundtrip ok`, both QEMU hosts. The verifiable e.os surface now has shell-boot breadth across all four shell-reachable modules: e.io (stdout + buffer round-trip), e.time (clocks + civil date), e.fmt (json/csv/ini), e.thread (spawn+join+group). C107 holds at its ~0.9 ceiling here: e.fs's remaining ops are flat-C106 Unsupported-by-design and its driver-boot fixtures (plus the C112-C114 rendering) need a matching toolchain, so further shell-boot breadth adds coverage without moving the score. PART (D4704): os.neperos.e declares the whole e.os fence, NeperOS runtime gains neper_hash_bytes/args/spawn stubs, shell/ident/host variants, target.Os.Neperos; 1,063 of 1,090 link fixtures compile for aarch64 neperos, 126 apps byte-identical. Compile-verified; neperos/src/map_test.e boot not yet run.

items.title: M3-04: e.gpu runtime surface: Device, Queue, Buf[T], launch, sync, barrier
items.evidence: `e.gpu` at `surface: partial`: `open`/`close`/`has`/`info`, `queue` and `queue_with`, `Buf[T]` as a generation-checked handle into a per-device table, `alloc`/`upload`/`write`/`download`/`release`/`len`, tokens with `done`/`wait`/`wait_for`, `sync`, `grid1/2/3`, and `gpu.launch[K]` as the third argument-pack intrinsic: the pack is checked against the kernel's parameters (`Buf[T]` for a device slice, a value of the parameter's type otherwise) and expands into a generated launcher per calling module, kernel and argument shape (D778). `gpu.barrier()` is the third device intrinsic recognised, legal only in a kernel's own body, lowered as the cut of the CPU build (D780). The fault buffer (D785): a failed tag, alignment, null, enum or bounds check in a kernel's CPU build writes the queue's one `FaultRecord` and ends the invocation, `sync`/`download` answer `Fault` once, `last_fault` answers the record. Presentation (D791): `Image`, `open_target`, `acquire`, `present`, `presented`, `resize` and `close_target`, offscreen on the CPU device. `[]Atomic[T]` launch parameters and both `gpu.memory_barrier` scopes already run in `link/gpu_vulkan_sync` on CPU and Vulkan (D1615). `queue_with` now uses a lazily allocated reusable Vulkan staging block, chunks writes by `block_bytes`, and frees it on close; CPU remains a direct copy (D1787). `link/gpu_staging` passes on CPU and two Windows Vulkan devices, and `gpu_vulkan_sync`, `gpu_cpu`, and `gpu_gaps` still pass there; the Linux CPU/no-device staging fixture passes. The device block now has a reentrant mutex covering queue, buffer and close operations; a short registry lock protects publication and token lookup, and CPU launches serialize their shared scheduler globals (D1788). `link/gpu_device_lock` passed ten Windows runs on CPU and both Vulkan devices, and passed Linux's CPU/no-device path. Existing GPU staging, sync, CPU, gaps and presentation fixtures pass on Windows; staging passes Linux's CPU/no-device path. Not yet: full-suite verification. The prior Windows suite reached its final function/type-renamed compiler image, which crashed with an access violation when compiling the original sources. Linux's bootstrap compiler rebuild restarted WSL even at pre-staging `afdc224b`. The current synchronous implementation reuses one staging block even when the configured bound allows more.

items.title: M3-05: device selection: devices, DeviceInfo/DeviceKind/DeviceKey, open_id, info
items.evidence: `devices` answers the bounded snapshot with the CPU device (`supported`, no stable key, capabilities copied into the caller's arena), `open` takes `.Cpu` index 0 and refuses other indices with `NoDevice` and other backends with `Unsupported`, `open_id` refuses a CPU key with `NoDevice` since the CPU has none, `info` copies the opening-time descriptor (D778). Not yet: Vulkan and CUDA enumeration, stable keys and `AmbiguousDevice`, memory capacity. items.title: Repeated diagnostics: fixtures and fingerprints for the codes that recur across a repair
items.evidence: Over 198 observed repairs in the transcripts (lang-stats.py, REPAIR table), a compile diagnostic is fixed in the next reply but only 15.7% of repairs took one edit, and 61.5% of consecutive failed builds repeat an error code from the failure before -- E-TYPE-0002 and the other kind-level codes cannot tell a second site from an unfixed first one. H31's cross-run fingerprints are T2; the v1 precursor is a fixture per recurring code that pins what the message must name (the span, the expected and found types, the binding) so a model can act on it once, tracked by lang-stats.py's repeat% and 1-edit%. Follow-on (D1898): the repeat metrics must cover OpenCode rows once the T037 harness split lands, or agent-visible progress stays Claude-only. Transcripts 2026-09-20..27 name the first fixtures: 134 builds failed on a compile code and 24 of 42 consecutive ones repeated a code. E-TYPE-9999 (29) printed an internal error name for its message -- `type checking failed: check.UnknownCallable`, `.ArgumentCount`, `.InvalidOperator`, `.Unsupported`, `.InvalidType`, `.MissingContext` -- naming no callee, count or operator; E-LEX-0003 (21) said `invalid token` for a malformed escape without naming the escape or the legal set (src/main.e print_parse_failure); E-NAME-9999 (8) said `unknown value name` without the name; E-TYPE-0003 (9) said `ret gives a different number of values` without the two counts; E-SYNTAX-9999 (9) said `unexpected ==` without what was expected. Each of those messages names its subject, the check.* names get codes of their own, and a fixture pins each. D1679 does that: ArgumentCount is E-TYPE-0005 (`take` takes 1 argument and this call gives 0) or E-TYPE-0007 (results discarded), UnknownCallable E-NAME-0004 with the callee, InvalidOperator E-TYPE-0006 with the operator and its expression, MissingContext E-TYPE-0001, InvalidType and Unsupported E-TYPE-0008/0009 quoting the statement; the unknown name, both ret counts, the bad escape with the legal set (and an unclosed literal, a control byte, a tab, a non-UTF-8 byte), and `; expected X` after `unexpected` where the parser knows X. The C bootstrap says the two messages its neper-0 fixtures pin, so self-host parity stays byte-equal. Pinned: seven check fixtures by text in both suites, the conformance and tools goldens, byte-equal on Linux. E-TYPE-0009 is reached by reject/not_supported, an assignment to an array range quoted by its first line (D1706, both suites). Not yet: lang-stats.py's repeat% and 1-edit% over transcripts written after D1679. Snapshot 2026-10-03 (14d): repeat% Claude 59.5 (was 61.5), Codex 70.0; 1-edit% identical across harnesses (54.3/53.5), so landed fixes transfer but recurrence does not; DeepSeek empty. Cross-run fingerprints remain the stuck point on both measured harnesses (D1904).

items.title: Work-stealing pool, parallel parse and codegen
items.evidence: the front end runs in waves of eight workers (D321); the modules are lowered, selected and written as artifacts on eight workers with checkers that share the declarations (D325); and the same workers check the bodies and build both inlining oracles first, each with a checker forked from the program's and importing the types of a body copied from another worker's oracle (D326). A two-million-line program builds cold in 7.6 s debug and 7.4 s release where it took 29 and 26, its body sweep 0.6 s where it took 1.9 (1.3 s where it took 5.7 in release), the settle nothing on a cold build and the lowering not re-checking what the sweep checked (D327), and the bootstrap runs a thread inline. The names are validated on the workers too (D328), the artifact writer copies bytes with one runtime call (D329), and the allocator, the digest and the lexer lost their last quadratic and per-byte costs (D330): a million-line program builds cold in 3.0 s on Windows and 3.4 s on Linux, warm in half a second; the link's per-artifact passes run on the workers too, with SHA-256 and CRC-32C in hardware where the CPU has them (D336): a million-line program builds warm in a quarter of a second, the compiler in 65 ms; what remains sequential is collecting the declarations, reachability and layout; the work is assigned statically, not stolen Stealing modules through a shared counter was built and measured, and reverted (D1578): the compiler's body phase is bound by its largest module (`check.e`), which no worker can split, and on sc500k the lowering lost the static schedule's balance (1.7-1.9 s against 1.3-1.5 s); the lever left is stealing a module's functions, across the D326/D327 coupling of checks to lowering. Moved to the end of the queue by the user's decision (D1579): what is left needs the declaration tables redesigned -- per-module tables merged in module order with every index relocated -- for at most the 152 ms of a 2.16 s sc500k build the declarations take (resolve 74 ms, the link from artifacts 130 ms), or function-level stealing across the D326/D327 coupling.

items.title: AES-GCM at OpenSSL's speed: AES and carry-less multiply instructions for e.crypto.aead
items.evidence: e.crypto.aead's AES-GCM is portable Neper, a bitsliced AES (BearSSL's aes_ct64) and a GHASH from masked integer products (ghash_ctmul64), D1645. Measured 2026-09-28 on the Core i5-12500H, sealing one TLS record: 11.6 us for 100 bytes and 702 us for 16 KB (23 MB/s), against OpenSSL's 0.73 us and 3.19 us (5.1 GB/s, through Python's cryptography 48, whose call overhead is included): 16 times slower on small records and 220 times on large ones. It bounds every TLS user: x.microsoft.tds scans SQL Server at 28-35% of the fastest language (D1643), where OpenSSL, Go and rustls run AES-NI and PCLMULQDQ. Closing the gap needs the back end to emit AESENC/AESENCLAST and PCLMULQDQ (x64) behind a CPU check with the portable path as the fallback, as SHA-256 and CRC-32C already are in the link (D336), then a GCM that keeps its expanded key and H powers across records (e.net.tls expands the key for every record today) and runs four to eight blocks in flight. Until then, the portable path's own lever is codegen: the same bitsliced rounds run at about 130 cycles a byte, several times BearSSL's in C. PART (D4300): four e.os intrinsics (cpu_features, aes_expand_key, aes_ctr, ghash_blocks; AES-NI and PCLMULQDQ on x86-64, aarch64 stubs answer none), e.crypto.aead takes the hardware path with the D1645 portable fallback; crypto_aead_hw passes vs portable GCM, OpenSSL and a bit-level GF(2^128) product on Windows and Linux x64; 16 KB seal ~1.8 GB/s vs OpenSSL ~5 GB/s on a quiet machine. Missing: 8-way interleave and fused CTR+GHASH, ARMv8 AES/PMULL, VAES.

items.title: NeperOS Dynamic, the server side: protocol, model, compile-and-repair, signing, many installed apps
items.evidence: Split from C124 (D2388): the device can verify, install, keep, ask about and launch a signed package and refuses what it did not declare. Acceptance: (1) the protocol over C117's TLS: a request carries the prompt, the app's identity and the device's API level; the answer carries the package (manifest, image, source, signature), streamed into the filesystem (a GET larger than httpc.e's 96 KB, with a request body); (2) a local test server with a canned model answer (no live model in the suite) that goes prompt to installed icon to launch to extension, as an installfixture; (3) the Dynamic app (D2238) calling it in place of its three templates and showing the stages from the server's progress; (4) the compile step on the server (the Neper compiler against the app kit, diagnostics fed back to the model until it builds or gives up readably), the scan before signing, a reproducible build, signing and revocation, an audit log; (5) many installed apps (the shell's single slot becomes a list from /apps), removal, update and rollback, and the manifest icon on the grid; (6) the NIR walk of the scanner (raw syscalls, undeclared capabilities, unbounded loops over input), with its report on the Details screen. Delivered by C124 and not to redo: D2383-D2388. PART (D4108): the build server streams stages, the 430 KB package is fetched without the httpc limit, checked and kept in /apps (dynamic_server); a restart adopts it and launches it (dynamic_server_again). Missing: many installed apps, update/rollback, removal, a live model. PART (D5103): many apps, update/rollback and removal pass. Remaining: live model, a fourth icon, the NIR scanner.

items.title: NeperOS Document remainder: PDF images and vectors, Office layout, pinch zoom, attachments

Delivered by C123 and not to redo: D2389-D2394. PART (D3801, D3802, D3804, D3805, D3809): painted PDF pages (rects, segments, text, colours, q/Q, cm), Word tables as grids, shebang detection, 12000-byte windows for big text files; QEMU rows document_pdf_paint, document_docx_table, document_big, document_shebang pass; fmt_pdf (23) and fmt_ooxml (39) pass. Pickup immediately after the chart cluster (L061, L068-L075). Versioned schema from the start; later slices extend it only by capability. items.title: Fast, small PNG encoding: dynamic Huffman, lazy matching and table CRC
items.evidence: Backlog from the chart benchmark (D2108, D2110). On the same 360x240 chart raster, e.fmt.png at .Balanced takes about 18 ms and writes 14,004 B, while zlib level 6 with the same filter-0 rows takes 1.74 ms for 11,283 B; rasterizing takes 2.0 ms, so the encoder is the whole PNG gap to matplotlib. e.algo.deflate writes fixed-Huffman blocks only (zlib restricted to fixed Huffman gives 12,903 B, so dynamic trees are worth about 1.6 KB here), has no lazy matching and restarts its 16-deep hash chain at every 32 KiB block (about 1.1 KB more), and e.fmt.png computes CRC-32 bit by bit. Done when: e.algo.deflate writes dynamic-Huffman blocks with lazy matching and a window that spans blocks, round-tripping through its own decoder and Python's zlib on a corpus; e.fmt.png uses a table-driven CRC; the chart benchmark's PNG pass is at least as fast as matplotlib's with files no larger than zlib level 6 on the same rows; both suites pass. Adaptive per-row filters are optional: Pillow's heuristic made this chart larger. PART (D2840): e.algo.deflate is zlib's lazy matcher (levels 6 and 9, 64 KiB window across blocks, stored/fixed/dynamic Huffman per 16383-token block); round-trips against Python zlib on 15 inputs x 3 levels, byte-identical to zlib 6 on four inputs, benchmark chart IDAT 11,277 B vs 11,283; e.fmt.png table CRC and deferred Adler. NOT MET: encoder alone about 5x C zlib (9.6 ms vs 1.7 ms on the 345,840-byte raster); the 'at least as fast as matplotlib' criterion is met only by a same-day comparison, not the nine-run protocol; adaptive PNG row filters not built. PART (D3700): png.encode_adaptive with libpng min-sum row filters and indexed output; fmt_png_adaptive byte-identical to Pillow on non-indexed cases, smaller than zlib 6 plus 1%. Missing: the deflate matcher is still ~4x C zlib, the nine-run protocol. PART (D4400): deflate/PNG encode about 2x faster with byte-identical output (callgrind 2.97 G -> ~1.5 G instructions, 800x500 adaptive ~225 -> ~120 ms wall, 48-case old/new differential identical, algo_deflate/fmt_png/fmt_png_adaptive/fmt_zlib/fmt_gzip pass). Still ~1.5-2x C zlib; nine-run protocol not run.

items.title: NeperOS Camera remainder: the sensor feed, video files, flash and exposure hardware, the QR reader

items.title: NeperOS Wallet remainder: encrypted storage, MRZ from an image, editing, camera scanning
items.evidence: Split from C121 (D2402): Wallet draws real QR and Code 128 symbols, validates its form with e.valid, and shows the newest Camera scan on a document. Acceptance: (1) the cards kept encrypted at rest under the Secure vault's master password (the vault module's derive/seal over the filesystem server), with no card number beyond the last four digits unless the user asks, loaded at start and fixture-tested through an encrypted round trip on a disk; (2) editing an existing card or document with the same validation; (3) Camera Scan mode feeding frames to e.barcode.qr_scan and offering the decoded text (a pass, a URL) to Wallet or the browser; (4) a machine-readable zone read from a scanned page (the OCR-B glyphs) and checked by e.valid.mrz_td3; (5) a scan stored with its own document instead of the newest one; (6) expiry checked against the clock. PART (D2447): a card's expiry is checked against the clock (Expired status; fixture wallet). Remaining: encrypted storage under the Secure master password, editing, Camera Scan mode, MRZ from an image, a scan per document. PART (D3807, D3808): cards sealed under the Secure vault key with an unlock screen, edit card for payment/bank/document, scan stored per document; disk chain secure_vault -> secure_vault_more -> secure_vault_again passes (12 records, expiry edited) and camera_scan -> camera_scan_more passes. Missing: Camera scan mode feeding qr_scan, MRZ from an image (no OCR-B recogniser), password prompt when no vault exists. PART (D4810-D4814): Camera Scan reads a QR into /scancode and Wallet adds it as a card (camera_scan, camera_scan_later); master-password create flow when no vault exists (wallet_vault_create, wallet_vault_create_again); save a card code as PNG to Files (wallet_image); MRZ read from a scan (wallet_mrz; mrz_read matches the reference reader exactly; gfx_vision +3 page reads). Remaining: a real OCR-B passport page untested (font unavailable), Camera 186x300 scan sheet too small for MRZ, TD1/TD2 zones, vault password change, opening a QR URL in the Browser.

items.title: NeperOS Maps remainder: map data, location, search and turn-by-turn navigation
items.evidence: Split from C130 (D2417): Maps routes over a small road graph with the library's Dijkstra and draws the way. Acceptance: (1) map data on the device: vector tiles or OpenStreetMap extracts rendered through e.gfx.scene with labels, icons, zoom levels and rotation, offline regions kept in Files, and drag and pinch (the touch layer needs both); (2) a location service (GPS and network location on the Pixel, a simulated provider under QEMU) with its permission in Settings (C126); (3) search by name and category with suggestions, place cards with hours and photos from the network; (4) routing for walking, cycling, driving and transit over the road graph with turn-by-turn instructions, rerouting and voice; (5) saved places, recent searches and a Home and Work shortcut shared with Wallet and Weather; (6) a fixture that loads a small offline region, finds a place and routes to it, checking the route length. Data source (user, 2026-10-11): free, non-Google maps -- OpenStreetMap (ODbL, attribution shown in the app): regional extracts (Geofabrik) or Protomaps/OpenFreeMap vector tiles cached in Files, the road graph built from the extract's highways, search from the extract's names (Nominatim only for light, identified use under its policy), no heavy use of tile.openstreetmap.org. PART (D2454): e.fmt.mvt decodes Mapbox Vector Tiles (fmt_mvt, 36 checks vs an independent encoder). Remaining: drawing tiles with styles and labels, offline regions, the road graph from the highway layer, search, location, navigation. PART (D3904): Maps fetches a zoom-14 vector tile, decodes it with e.fmt.mvt and draws roads, water and POI names with the ODbL line; maps_tile passes against an independent tile encoder. Missing: tile pyramid and panning, offline regions, road graph, search, location, navigation. PART (D4920-D4923): tile pyramid with pan and zoom, offline regions in Files, Nominatim search plus OSRM route with steps, location via the sensor server; rows maps_pyramid, maps_offline(+_again), maps_search, maps_location. Remaining: road graph from an extract, walking/cycling/transit, saved places, rerouting and voice, rotation/pinch.

items.title: NeperOS Level remainder: fast sensor stream, self-test, orientation modes, feedback

Remaining: the 50 Hz stream from the sensor server, Level's modes, readings and feedback, a recorded-trace fixture. items.title: NeperOS Steps remainder: background counting, history, profile, notifications

Acceptance: (1) counting in the background at a low-power sensor rate from the sensor server (C161), with the run and walk classification shown; (2) the history of days, weeks and months in storage (C125), the goal, streaks and a weekly report; (3) calories from the user's height and weight (a profile in Settings, C126) rather than a fixed figure per step; (4) a notification when the goal is reached through the status server and a widget on the home screen; (5) a fixture that replays a recorded accelerometer walk and checks the count within two per cent. items.title: NeperOS AI remainder: streaming, keys in Secure, conversations, files and tools
items.evidence: Split from C141 (D2430): AI sends a conversation to a provider and shows the answer. Acceptance: (1) the reply streamed (server-sent events) into the bubble, which needs the network layer to read a response incrementally and the compositor's ticks to keep arriving during a request; (2) the API key kept in Secure (C170's store), never in memory longer than a request, and a cheap key check on Save; (3) conversations kept in storage (C125) with titles, search, rename and delete, system prompts, and temperature and token limits as settings; a configurable host for the local server; (4) images from Camera and Photos, files from Files and documents from Document as inputs, and the reply's code blocks highlighted; (5) a tool-use loop so a conversation can call other apps through capabilities, each with a confirmation; (6) a fixture against a mock server that streams a reply and checks the error paths for each provider's status codes. Not queued here: voice mode, image generation. PART (D2453): e.fmt.sse, an incremental Server-Sent Events reader (fmt_sse, 46 checks vs the standard's algorithm on whole streams and every prefix). Remaining: incremental reads from the network server over TLS, streaming into the bubble, keys in Secure, conversations, files, tools. PART (D4102-D4103): reply streams into the bubble over TLS (ai_stream), key checked and sealed in the Secure vault (ai_secure, ai_secure_again), conversations and options kept. Missing: images/files as inputs, tool-use loop, per-provider error-path fixture. PART (D5101, D5102): attachments, tool loop and per-provider error words are committed with a host test server; rows ai_err_anthropic/openai/google, ai_attach, ai_tools are NOT yet run on QEMU. Remaining: those boots.

Not queued here: editing, annotation, signing. The prompt and server pieces follow in C124. Not queued here: a store, sharing. items.title: NeperOS Clock remainder: a background ringer with the app closed
items.evidence: Split from C145 (D2433): the Clock's alarms, timer and stopwatch persist in /clock. items.title: NeperOS clipboard remainder: Paste in every field, a lifetime setting, clear on lock
items.evidence: Split from C148 (D2435): the clipboard holds text, Secure copies to it and AI pastes from it. items.title: NeperOS settings recipients remainder: audio, fingerprint, radios, battery
items.evidence: Split from C149 (D2436): notification permission is enforced at the status service. Acceptance: (1) an audio server (virtio-sound or a software mixer behind e.audio) that takes the media, ring and alarm volumes and Vibrate from the settings server, with a fixture on QEMU; (2) a fingerprint or biometric unlock path on the lock screen, or a recorded sensor in the test boots, honouring the Fingerprint switch; (3) Bluetooth and Hotspot recipients in the network stack (a link layer that can be switched), gated like Airplane mode; (4) a real battery provider posting to the status service, and per-app permissions (camera, location, storage) as values per app; (5) apps hold a notification capability so they can post as themselves through OP_POST_APP. PART: lock_fingerprint, settings_permission and the audio mixer/ringer/notification paths exercised by clock_ring pass. Missing: Bluetooth/Hotspot recipients, a real battery provider (status_server takes a recorded 78 %). items.title: gRPC remainder: server side, deadlines and stubs from .proto descriptors
items.evidence: Split from L101 (D2646): e.net.http2 and the e.net.grpc client protocol exist and are checked against hpack/h2 and recorded grpcio transcripts. Acceptance: (1) a server side over e.net.http2 (unary, then streaming); (2) deadlines, retries and message compression; (3) the gRPC-over-HTTP/3 binding on e.net.http3 frames; (4) a TLS dial helper; (5) stub generation from .proto descriptors (e.fmt.protobuf needs a descriptor reader first) with typed request and response messages. PART (D2923): e.net.grpcserver (preface, SETTINGS, HPACK, flow control, request events, flow-controlled responses, trailers-only, deadlines, resets) and e.net.grpccodec (gzip/deflate/identity decompression) checked with grpcio against a live loopback server (14 calls). NOT DONE: retries and backoff, gRPC over HTTP/3, a TLS dial helper, send-side compression wiring, stub generation (e.fmt.protobuf has no descriptor reader). PART (D3004-D3008): send-side compression (net_grpccompress, decoded by Python gzip/zlib), e.fmt.protodesc descriptor reader (32 cases vs protobuf MessageToDict), typed stubs e.fmt.protomsg/e.net.grpcstub (242 Python-serialised instances round trip), e.net.grpcretry (gRFC A6 vs a Python model), e.net.grpctls dial helper. Missing: gRPC over HTTP/3, retry wired into a transport loop, hedging, perAttemptRecvTimeout. PART (D3401): e.net.grpccall retry and hedging loop over e.net.grpc with deadline and per-attempt timeout; net_grpccall 331 runs, 60 against live grpcio, 271 against an independent A6 model. Missing: HTTP/3, transparent retries, a socket run; per_attempt_ns has no live oracle. PART (D4601): transparent retries (REFUSED_STREAM reset, GOAWAY below the stream id) first one per call, not counted or throttled; net_grpccall 401 cases (41 goaway scripts agree with live grpcio; the REFUSED_STREAM half is the gRFC model, grpcio treats it as UNAVAILABLE); 15/15 loopback socket scenarios agree with the model. Missing: HTTP/3 (no oracle), hedging combined with transparent retry has no vector, per_attempt_ns has no grpcio oracle.

items.evidence: Plan docs/browser-progress.html, decisions D5114 to D5122. Acceptance: (1) tracker phase P0 (0.1 to 0.8): oracle frozen, html5lib, WPT reftest, pixel-probe and render-tool harnesses, Ahem asset, baselines; (2) P1 parse and style core: 1.1 to 1.14, html5lib at least Dart's 1549 of 1791; (3) P2 2.1 to 2.3 block and inline layout over e.text; (4) P3 3.1 to 3.6 and 3.11 display list, scene tiling, backgrounds, borders, text, images; (5) P4 4.1 and 4.2 loader and HTTP/1.1; (6) 7.0 lib/e/ui/html_view.e shows a static document over e.fmt.dom, e.fmt.css.style, e.fmt.css.layout and e.fmt.css.paint (D5123: reusable parts are library modules, not e.web); 7.1 lib/e/ui/browser.e builds on it, loads an HTTP(S) page, scrolls, follows links; Hacker News within the pixel tolerance of the Dart golden. Not yet: everything except 0.1, most of 0.3, 0.6a, 1.1 to 1.3, 1.7 and 1.13a to 1.13d. PART (2026-10-16): 0.6a html5lib runner done (tests/browser/html5lib/run.sh) 1.1 to 1.3 done (D5124) 1.7 done (D5125, e.fmt.dom with fixture fmt_dom) 1.13a to 1.13f done (D5126, D5127: sheet loader with all at-rules but nesting, user agent sheet; fixtures css_sheet, css_ua) and 1.13a to 1.13d done (D5126, e.fmt.css.style and e.fmt.css.expand with fixture css_style: expansion before ranking, typed computed values, inheritance, var()): e.fmt.html is the WHATWG tokenizer and tree builder, 1791 of 1791 html5lib cases against Dart's 1549 (it was 572), floor enforced by run.sh; the WPT reftest runner, pixel-probe and render tool wait for the layout and paint layers; 0.1 done (D5114 to D5123); 0.3 Dart oracle frozen: vaper tag dart-oracle-final at 8e0c4e9, a record/replay capture tool, six sites (Hacker News, example.com, Wikipedia Comparison_of_web_browsers with 12317 nodes, MDN, craigslist, abv.bg) captured with PNG, node and display-list goldens, each replay byte-identical twice, in tests/browser/oracle with a README; the jQuery page set and the licence decision before committing the stores remain. PART: landed pieces that M1 reuses, not yet checked against the oracle: e.fmt.html, e.fmt.css.syntax/selector/match/cascade/container, e.gfx.cssvalue (L038, L040), e.fmt.woff and woff2 (D2346), e.net.policy and ssrf (D2351). Status 2026-11-03 (branch browser-conformance, tracker rows of P0+P1): 10 done, 8 partial, 9 todo of 28; score is the mean with partial counted as half. Handover fold 2026-11-19: 7.3 needs a focus path into the page (page.focus_node honoured by dom_js, recommended; owner decision pending), Tab order, Enter activation, focus ring, text input via Edit and IME, clipboard, kinetic scroll, scrollbars, cursor; 7.6 needs accessibility relations and live regions in e.fmt.html.accessible and html_view. Verification gap (handover fold 2026-11-19): the nested scope > region > semantics > canvas page area of examples/browser/main.e is compile-verified only; nobody has looked at a window. Look at it before scoring 7.3 above compile level. Known app ceilings and one unlocated defect: text layout memory looks quadratic in text length (the loop was never located; a long untitled address exhausted the 16 MB frame arena); a typed or pasted omnibox address over 400 bytes is cut (deliberate ceiling; omni_clipped and omni_real keep the full address only while unedited); a long address is drawn across the toolbar buttons. Web (wasm32-wasi) target: scripts, clicks and scrolling were never verified and only two Jost fonts are seeded (run recipe in memory neper-browser-wpt-recipe).

items.title: Browser M2: modern CSS layout
items.evidence: Plan docs/browser-progress.html. Needs L166. Acceptance: (1) P2 2.4 to 2.15: floats, positioned and sticky, tables, flex, grid, multicolumn, intrinsic sizing, overflow, transforms, replaced elements, form controls, hit testing and geometry; (2) P3 3.4, 3.5, 3.8, 3.9 gradients, shadows, clip-path, mask, filters; (3) 9.2 WPT CSS reftests reproduce at least Dart's 116 of 122 and the six known failures are triaged; (4) the Dart layout pixel-probe expectations carried over as fixtures and green. Not yet: all of it. Status 2026-11-03 (branch browser-conformance, tracker rows of P2+P3): 4 done, 21 partial, 16 todo of 41; score is the mean with partial counted as half. Handover fold 2026-11-19: the uncommitted sideways-lr frame in lib/e/fmt/css/layout.e (writing-modes 638 to 650) needs flexbox 650 and grid 1038 sweeps with zero new FAIL before commit, else revert and record; then sideways-lr counter-clockwise paint (paint.e ~968), flexbox safe overflow (parse_align drops safe, 001..005), grid rtl subgrid line-names-012, css-text piece loop (break-spaces 210/320, letter-spacing 3/29, hanging-punctuation 6/21), css-content element replacement 6/14, sizing, multicol, css-sizing re-measure. Never build a sub-manifest by grepping MANIFEST.txt (false green); use --only. Failing-cluster leads (handover fold 2026-11-19, leads not a ledger): css-flexbox flexbox-writing-mode 9, balance/* ~20 (balance-002 body max-content 51 vs 60), aspect-ratio-intrinsic-size 6, flexbox-min-width-auto, flexbox-definite-sizes, baseline-*, -left-002/-right-002; css-writing-modes table-cell-align 6, block-plaintext 5, bidi-override 5, bidi-isolate-override 5, ch-units-vrl 4, available-size 4, table-progression-vrl/vlr/slr ~8, vertical-alignment-*; css-grid baseline -002/-008, grid-lanes subgrid ~116, track-sizing 51, alignment 50, abspos 42, intrinsic-sizing 33. Grid baseline (rounds 256-262, REFUTES the earlier claim that the row-baseline pass exists only in layout_lanes_rows): it exists and is correct in layout_grid_inner, so do not build one. The 30 self-baseline files are blocked on vertical-writing-mode inline-block layout in a float (the reference is a different container shape, our grid is right), so no grid-baseline code can flip them. grid-baseline-align-001 is an inline-grid abspos static position lacking bx: guard !pb.inline_level at the static-position code; a plain static_x = pad_x + bb.x collapses css-grid/alignment 96 to 41 because pad_x absorbs the grid-area and root adjustments. The question of recording the baseline family as dropped is open in docs/open-questions.md. Block-ellipsis is decided (D7724: keep the clamped-line prefix, ellipsis-alone references accepted as an older encoding). content: url() on a pseudo-element (css-content 6/14): layout.Measure has no url_size (page, runners and app each construct it); gen_pseudo creates a .Replaced box that paint_atomic would paint with its border, the url resolves and the SVG has a 100x100 intrinsic size, but no IFC container lists the box (no ATOM trace for abh=120), so the next step is to print its parent right after append(l, parent_box, rb) in gen_pseudo. Sideways-lr frame mechanics (flow_frame code 3, remap_rect 3 to 0 with the inline axis reversed, root laid out with fi = ch) live only in the uncommitted layout.e diff: do not discard it; the revert is `git checkout -- lib/e/fmt/css/layout.e` after running flexbox and grid and diffing the FAIL lists. Harness-unmeasurable failure classes are not debt (memory neper-browser-wpt-recipe). A subgrid must ignore its own width: the row axis zeroes rmin/rmax near layout.e 8717, the column axis has no equivalent. grid-lanes is largely implemented (294 of 858); the real cluster is subgrid-inside-lanes (grid-subgridded 134, track-sizing/auto 95, intrinsic-sizing 40, dense 27). line-names-012: an inner subgrid inherits grid-column: 2 / span 2 from a shared stylesheet and an rtl subgrid places it on the physically left track (look at layout_grid_inner placement of a clamped 2 / span 2 child). sideways-lr is approximated (layout runs in frame 2, asymmetric top/bottom edges mapped as vertical-lr); an uncommitted sideways-lr change sits in lib/e/fmt/css/layout.e. Refuted: break-spaces needs a piece-loop redesign shared with letter-spacing (~136 files), hanging-punctuation (U+3000 is not a text piece), the CSS2 syntax family (at-charset/character-encoding need an HTTP header). Still failing: css-overflow line-clamp (113) and scroll-markers (44), css-multicol 186/402, contain-intrinsic-size 008, 012, 014, 017, 020, 023, 025, 027. Open leads (handover fold 2026-11-20; refuted attempts with numbers are in memory neper-browser-dead-ends): CSS2 syntax 233/275: uri-* lose a valid declaration downstream of sheet.load, in rank_expanded/cascade; escapes-014..016 accept " yellow" through a colour path other than parse_color_value; hanging-punctuation: U+3000 is dropped in the scan (out.lead) before the fragment loop; flex balance-002 needs the body width (ref 86, ours 51) traced from where it is decided; grid-lanes subgrid t012 (15 cases) is the placement of 2 / span 2 in an rtl subgrid; text-transform/letter-spacing/hanging-punctuation need @font-face WOFF loading in the reftest runner.

items.title: Browser M4: JavaScript engine and DOM bindings
items.evidence: Plan docs/browser-progress.html, decision D5115. Needs L166; engine work (5.1 to 5.16) can start in parallel with L167. Acceptance: (1) P5 5.1 to 5.16: parser, compiler, VM, heap and GC, object model, builtins, ECMAScript RegExp, Promise and microtasks, modules, test262 runner with feature-gated pass targets, benchmarks against QuickJS; (2) P6 6.1 to 6.8 and 6.14 bindings: DOM, CSSOM, events, timers, fetch, storage, forms; (3) 6.17 iframes; (4) jQuery 3.5.1 initialises, AJAX re-renders, timers and events work, getBoundingClientRect feeds layout; (5) 9.4 test262 targets, 9.6 real-site sweep including JS-app pages. Not yet: all of it. Status 2026-11-03 (branch browser-conformance, tracker rows of P5+P6): 0 done, 26 partial, 15 todo of 41; score is the mean with partial counted as half. Handover fold 2026-11-19: script side: creation-realm field on html.Node for cross-realm DOM, new Document().appendChild(createElement("html")) stack overflow, per-select selectOptions cache, interpreter stale Frame/Program pointer (wpt-gate chunks at 40 as workaround); WICG proposals (processing-instruction-attributes, partial-updates) and Trusted Types await a decision. Script-side triage (handover fold 2026-11-19): dom/events single-activation-behavior 91 of 132; ParentNode-querySelector-All 48; namespaced-attribute-mutations 12; test262 40,458 of 40,938 (runner t262.e); DOM 11235 of 11664. Open gaps: Trusted Types, remaining scoped registries (~50), document named properties, no SVGElement interface or SVG animation, setFormValue submission, OpaqueRange, moveBefore state loss, testdriver actions, html/browsers/history, innerText getter and ::first-line/::first-letter, cross-realm DOM (~39 subtests), partial-updates (~14). Leads (handover fold 2026-11-20): select-element needs a tree-order selectOptions walk with a per-select cache before the last-selected-option-wins rule (ordering constraint and the cumulative interpreter abort, threshold 117 to 140 files, in memory neper-browser-dead-ends); ParentNode-querySelector-All 48 = :link/:visited, :target, :root, namespace selectors, ::slotted, unclosed bracket; select[i] needs legacy-object wrappers; script-side fixes get a regression in dom_mixins (web_shell fixture).

items.title: e.ui in a browser: a real phone's virtual keyboard and IME
items.evidence: Android Chrome checked by hand (D5890, D5891: suggestion replacement, touch hold, drag selection, toolbar); iPhone simulator (iOS 17.5 Mobile Safari, .github/workflows/ios-sim.yml, D5900) passes typing, Backspace and the hold toolbar; a real iPhone and a composing keyboard are still unchecked. Needs a device. Prepared: `node scripts/serve-wasm.mjs --isolated --host 0.0.0.0` and open /tests/wasm/browser/phone_probe.html on the phone (a plain field that logs key, composition, paste, visualViewport and scroll events; Report copies the log) to answer checks 1-5 before touching ui_counter. D5821 lists what the mobile preset did and did not show (synthetic composition events, the textarea at 16 px not scrolling or zooming). Serve tests/wasm/browser/ui_counter.html over HTTPS or a LAN address with scripts/serve-wasm.mjs --isolated (a secure context is needed for crossOriginIsolated and the clipboard) and check on iOS Safari and Android Chrome: (1) tapping the Name field opens the keyboard and neither zooms nor scrolls the page; (2) typed letters, Backspace and Enter arrive once each; (3) composition with a CJK keyboard (pinyin or kana) delivers the committed text once, with no duplicate after compositionend and none while composing; (4) the clipboard: paste from the system menu reaches the program, and Ctrl+C in the program writes navigator.clipboard, with the permission prompt answered either way; (5) visualViewport resizes when the keyboard opens and the canvas stays usable (decide whether the window follows it); (6) a physical keyboard on a tablet still works. Fix what fails in lib/wasm/window.js; window_visible is separate.

items.title: OpenGL 16: the Android target, executable form
items.evidence: Done 2026-10-27 (D5896, D5900): emit-executable ... x64 android and aarch64 android write the Linux image typed ET_DYN for /system/bin/linker64, with Bionic library names (libc.so) plus libdl.so and liblog.so; arm64 Android images always carry a dynamic segment, and arm64 atomics are LDAXR/STLXR loops (ARMv8.0). Android is linux to every module and variant, so no os.android.e was needed (neither Bionic nor SELinux refused anything run so far). scripts/run-android.ps1 [-Arch aarch64] runs hello, advanced, gpu_cpu, gpu_fault_bounds, x_khronos_gl_load, x_khronos_gl_headless, atomic_ops, atomic_threads and channel_threads on the SDK's Android 15 x86_64 emulator for both architectures, all passing, with GLES 3.0 drawing and reading back. Remaining: e.gpu compute on a device with GLES 3.1+. The emulator stops at 3.0 on this host: SwiftShader, -gpu host on the Iris Xe (draws there too) and -feature GLESDynamicVersion all report ro.opengles.version 196608, and -feature GuestAngle does not boot, so this needs a real phone. Design docs/opengl-plan.md, D5884. Needs T047. Acceptance: --target android-x64 and android-a64 emit a PIE ELF for /system/bin/linker64 with DT_NEEDED libc.so, libdl.so and liblog.so; os.android.e is os.linux.e without what Bionic and SELinux refuse; the executable runs under adb shell on the x86_64 emulator, and T047's fixtures pass there on GLES. Recipe: scripts/run-android.ps1 -Arch aarch64 gpu_gl gpu_gl_exact gpu_gl_narrow gpu_gl_subgroup on a real phone; fold into C213.

items.title: Browser: ad and tracker blocking on every request
items.evidence: PART: e.net.fetch.Config.block_hosts and allow_hosts (from e.net.policy.parse_filter_list: ||host^ rules and @@||host^ exceptions) refuse any request that has a referrer (a subresource) to a listed host or its subdomains with BlockedByFilter before connecting, count them in Client.blocked, never filter the document, and an empty list blocks nothing; examples/browser reads an optional neper-browser.filters list; net_fetch_filter pins listed host, subdomain, unlisted host, document, exception and no list. `$third-party` rules block only requests from another site (hosts equal or one a subdomain of the other count as one site) and page.blocked_count reports the refusals since a page began loading; net_fetch_filter pins both. Request-type options (`$script`, `$image`, `$stylesheet`, `$xhr`, `$font`, `$document`, and `~type` negations) apply too: Request.dest is set by the page for script, stylesheet, image, font and xhr fetches and a typed rule blocks only those types (net_fetch_filter pins script-only, ~image and untyped). `$domain=a.com|~b.com` limits a rule to pages on the listed domains (net_fetch_filter pins listed, unlisted and excluded pages). `||host/path^` limits a rule to URLs under that path (net_fetch_filter pins both). Still open: a profile switch to turn blocking off. e.net.policy already parses Adblock Plus filter lists (parse_filter_list). Nothing applies them when a page loads. Acceptance: e.web.page asks the parsed rules before each subresource and script fetch (document, script, image, stylesheet, xhr, font types and the third-party flag known to the loader), a blocked request fails as blocked and is counted per page, the main document is never blocked, rules load from the profile and can be switched off, and a fixture with a blocked tracker script, an allowed first-party script and an exception rule pins all three outcomes.
